content:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated ELB 5xx rate observed in eu-west-1 (azc). Auto-detect triggered at 2024-04-23T09:00Z.
ops-bot: Summary metrics: ELB 5xx -> 9% of requests, latency p95 up 220ms, healthy host count dropping in azc.
mike_oncall: ack. paging in infra + network. I'm on it, digging into dashboards.
sara_infra: I'm seeing simultaneous ENI churn in azc based on host-level logs (kernel ARP retries). LB health checks failing to TCP in the same AZ.
kevin_net: Confirmed from VPC flow logs — asymmetric egress for instances in azc to the NAT gateways (packets show retransmits). No obvious ACL changes.
mike_oncall: Any Route53 anomalies?
kevin_net: Route53 is normal but we see a small increase in DNS TTL-stale cache hits; however the traffic imbalance looks like network path degradation inside azc causing ELB to mark targets unhealthy.
emily_sre: Can we mitigate by shifting weights away from azc for regional entry? We have weighted Route53 record for inference.redwood.ai (weights per AZ-region).
sara_infra: Yes. Recommend immediate weight shift: reduce azc pool to 0 and move weight to azb + a fallback in us-west-2. That'll reduce customer impact quickly.
mike_oncall: OK, doing a controlled weighted shift to azb and us-west-2. I'll keep a small canary (5%) to monitor for false positives.
kevin_net: Before we shift, note that some customers are pinned via dedicated endpoints to azc — those won't follow DNS weight. We'll need targeted routing or connection drain.
jake_support: Support: which customers will be affected by weight shift? Need list for notification.
sara_infra: Pulling mapping of dedicated pools -> azc. Quick list: cust-42 (high traffic), cust-77 (background batch jobs). Estimated 12% of total requests routed to azc across the region.
mike_oncall: Initiating Route53 change now. Command we ran:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1ABCDEF --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-azc","Weight":0,"TTL":60}}]}'
```
ops-bot: Change submitted, status PENDING.
emily_sre: After weight shift, watch for backlog at us-west-2. We should pre-scale standby hosts and increase ELB capacity.
sara_infra: Spinning up additional dedicated instances in us-west-2 and azb, increasing target group capacity by +30%.
kevin_net: AWS support ticket opened (case# 1234567890). They see internal net path anomalies in eu-west-1 azc; escalation to networking team.
mike_oncall: Observability: token-level latency now back down for majority of requests; 5xx reduced from 9% -> 1.5% in 12m since weight shift.
jake_support: Notifying affected customers: drafting message to cust-42 and cust-77 about degraded connectivity and in-progress mitigation.
kevin_net: We also observed elevated EBS attach/retry errors for a small subset of instances in azc — seems correlated with ENI instability. Likely root cause is rack-level networking flap.
emily_sre: Good catch. For dedicated pools pinned to azc, propose graceful drain + migrate. Run drain with `connection-drain: 300s` and trigger instance replacement.
sara_infra: Applying instance replacement for pinned pools: creating new instances in azb and migrating state via snapshot/replicas.
mike_oncall: Customer impact summary for pager: Partial 5xx/latency for ~12% traffic in eu-west-1, impacting both hosted API and some dedicated capacity customers. Severity: P2 (regional degraded).
jake_support: Support notification sent to cust-42; they acknowledged and asked for ETA. I replied: mitigation in progress, validation within 30–45m, will provide update in 1h.
ops-bot: Incident timeline note appended to thread.
emily_sre: Next steps: continue replacement in azc, monitor AWS updates, prepare for possible cross-region failover if AZ doesn't stabilize.
kevin_net: AWS network team reports they're seeing intermittent fiber uplink flaps to one rack in azc; repair ETA unknown.
mike_oncall: Since ETA unknown, schedule a controlled cross-AZ failover for remaining traffic: update routing so that dedicated endpoints with fallback policies prefer azb / us-west-2.
sara_infra: Implemented failover for dedicated endpoints via our control plane — traffic for pinned pools will gracefully reconnect within drain window.
jake_support: Logged affected customers and post-notes to status.redwood.ai page. Copying the message to sales for high-touch customers.
emily_sre: Handing incident to night on-call at 18:00Z (mike -> emily). Handoff notes: weight shift in place, AWS case open #1234567890, EBS attach errors mitigated by instance replacement in progress, monitor for residual 5xx.
mike_oncall: Handoff ack. Leaving a checklist: 1) Monitor ELB healthy host count 2) Confirm DNS propagation 3) Continue instance replacement in azc 4) Coordinate with AWS if hardware replacement needed 5) Postmortem owner: sara_infra.
emily_sre: Ack. I'll own until stabilized and then open a postmortem.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status: mitigated (traffic shifted, dedicated pool migration started). Final metrics: 5xx -> ~0.6% region-wide.
mike_oncall: Thanks team. Closing pager rotation for this incident; leaving thread for follow-ups.
sara_infra: Postmortem TODOs: root cause confirmation with AWS, improve dedicated pool fallback automation, add runbook for ENI-ARP flaps.
jake_support: I'll follow up with affected customers with final notes once postmortem is posted.
ops-bot: Thread archived to incidents log.
